title: Modules and Privacy
goal: Organize code with mod and understand default privacy boundaries.

sections.text: You use `mod` to group functions, structs, and traits under a named namespace.

sections.caption: `pub` makes the function visible outside the module.

sections.text: Items in Rust are private by default. A parent module cannot see private items inside a child module.

sections.caption: Call module items with the `::` path separator.

sections.text: Use the `pub` keyword to grant visibility to outer modules. If a module itself is private, its public items cannot be reached from outside.

explanation: Organize code with mod and understand default privacy boundaries.
